business_model.claim: Star Group, L.P. operates as a single reportable operating segment providing home heating oil, propane, and heating-related services.
quotes: Star Group, L.P. (“Star” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) is a home heating oil and propane distributor and services provider with one reportable operating segment that principally provides heating related services to residential and commercial customers.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025, total sales comprised approximately 63% from home heating oil and propane, 18% from other petroleum products such as diesel and gasoline, and 19% from the installation and repair of heating and air conditioning equipment and ancillary services.
quotes: During fiscal 2025, total sales were comprised of approximately 63% from home heating oil and propane, 18% from other petroleum products, the majority of which is diesel and gasoline, and 19% from the installation and repair of heating and air conditioning equipment and ancillary services.

business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2025, Star served approximately 406,400 full service and 63,200 delivery-only home heating oil and propane customers across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic U.S. regions, along with approximately 27,700 gasoline and diesel customers and 20,200 natural gas and other service contract customers.
quotes: We are a home heating oil and propane distributor and service provider to residential and commercial customers whose primary use is to heat their homes and buildings in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic U.S. regions.
As of September 30, 2025, we sold home heating oil and propane to approximately 406,400 full service residential and commercial customers and 63,200 customers on a delivery only basis.
We also sell gasoline and diesel fuel to approximately 27,700 customers.

We install, maintain, and repair heating and air conditioning equipment and to a lesser extent provide these services outside of our heating oil and propane customer base including 20,200 service contracts for natural gas and other heating systems.

business_model.claim: Star's full service home heating oil and propane base is 96% residential and 4% commercial, with approximately 277,000 customers (59%) located in New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut.
quotes: Our full service home heating oil and propane customer base is comprised of 96% residential customers and 4% commercial customers.
Approximately 277,000 of these customers, or 59%, are located in the New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut.

business_model.claim: Star operates a margin-based model that prices liquid products at a per-gallon margin over wholesale costs, with residential customers choosing variable, ceiling, or fixed-price plans and 93% of full service customers receiving automatic deliveries.
quotes: It is common practice in our business to price our liquid products to customers based on a per gallon margin over wholesale costs.
Our business is a “margin-based” business in which gross profit depends on the excess of sales prices per gallon over supply costs per gallon.

We also offer several pricing alternatives to our residential home heating oil customers, including a variable price (market based) option and a price-protected option, the latter of which either sets the maximum price or a fixed price that a customer will pay.
Approximately 93% of our full service residential and commercial home heating oil and propane customers automatically receive deliveries based on prevailing weather conditions.

business_model.claim: Home heating oil and propane generated $481.1 (table in millions) of gross profit at $1.7022 per gallon in fiscal 2025, compared with $44.1 (table in millions) at $0.3559 per gallon for motor fuel and other petroleum products and $37.7 million combined gross profit from installations and services.
quotes: We realized a combined gross profit from services and installations of $37.7 million for fiscal 2025 compared to a combined gross profit of $33.9 million for fiscal 2024, a $3.8 million increase in profitability.

business_model.claim: For the 9 months ended June 30, 2026, Star recorded total sales of $ 1,664,042 (table in thousands), comprising $ 1,404,780 (table in thousands) in product sales and 259,262 (table in thousands) in installations and services sales.

Approximately 80% of Star's annual home heating oil and propane volume is sold during the October through March peak-heating season, resulting in net income in the first and second fiscal quarters and net losses in the third and fourth fiscal quarters.
quotes: During the peak-heating season of October through March, sales of home heating oil and propane historically have represented approximately 80% of our annual volume sold.

As a result, we generally realize net income in our first and second fiscal quarters and net losses during our third and fourth fiscal quarters and we expect that the negative impact of seasonality on our third and fourth fiscal quarter operating results will continue.

business_model.claim: Year-to-year temperature swings directly drive volume, as 11.5 percent colder temperatures during fiscal 2026 year-to-date through June 30, 2026 helped lift home heating oil and propane volume by 3.3 percent to 271.2 million gallons.
quotes: The volume of home heating oil and propane sold during the first nine months of fiscal 2026 increased by 8.6 million gallons, or 3.3 percent, to 271.2 million gallons, reflecting colder temperatures and the additional volume provided from acquisitions, more than offsetting net customer attrition and other factors.

Temperatures in Star’s geographic areas of operation fiscal year-to-date were 11.5 percent colder than during the prior-year period and 2.9 percent colder than normal, as reported by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

business_model.basis: stated in P3, P4, and P6
business_model.claim: Top-line product revenue fluctuates with wholesale product costs passed through in selling prices, though higher retail prices can prompt customer conservation and increase gross customer losses.
quotes: For fiscal 2025, product sales decreased $11.2 million, or 0.8%, to $1,437.6 million, compared to $1,448.8 million in fiscal 2024, due to a decrease in average selling prices that was slightly offset by an increase in total volume sold of 6.3%.

For the nine months ended June 30, 2026, Star reported an 8.3 percent increase in total revenue to $1.7 billion, reflecting higher product volumes sold and an increase in selling prices in response to higher wholesale product costs.
Our customers are sensitive to wholesale product cost increases, and this often leads to customer conservation and increased gross customer losses.

business_model.claim: Star faces ongoing customer attrition in a declining retail heating oil market, losing 19,600 accounts net (4.7%) in fiscal 2025, including an estimated (1.3%) lost to natural gas and electricity conversions.
quotes: The retail home heating oil industry is mature, with total market demand expected to decline in the foreseeable future due to conversions to natural gas and electricity, availability of other alternative energy sources and the installations of more fuel efficient heating systems.

For fiscal 2025, the Company lost 19,600 accounts (net), or 4.7%, of its home heating oil and propane customer base, compared to 16,600 accounts lost (net), or 4.2%, of its home heating oil and propane customer base, during fiscal 2024.
During fiscal 2025, we estimate that we lost (1.3%) of our home heating oil and propane accounts to natural gas and electricity conversions versus (1.4%) for fiscal 2024 and (1.6%) for fiscal 2023.

business_model.claim: To offset industry decline, Star relies on acquisitions and service growth, spending approximately $80.5 million on acquisitions in fiscal 2025 while acquisitions contributed 25.1 (table in millions of gallons) of heating oil and propane volume and $22.6 million of installation and service sales.
quotes: Therefore, our ability to maintain our business or grow within the industry is dependent on the acquisition of other retail distributors, the success of our marketing programs, and the growth of our other service offerings.
During fiscal 2025, the Company acquired one heating oil business and three propane businesses for approximately $80.5 million.
Acquisitions | 25.1

The increase was driven by $22.6 million of sales generated from recent acquisitions, and the remainder was driven by a concerted effort to expand these offerings to our customers as well as annual price increases.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Cost of product ($912.4 million in fiscal 2025) is driven by wholesale liquid fuel prices tied to diesel fuel, supply constraints, futures backwardation, and state biofuel mandates that raised minimum biodiesel blends in July 2025 to 10% in New York and Connecticut and 20% in Rhode Island.
quotes: For fiscal 2025, cost of product decreased $68.4 million, or 7.0%, to $912.4 million, compared to $980.8 million for fiscal 2024, due to a decrease in wholesale product cost of $0.3199 per gallon, or 12.5%, slightly offset by an increase in total volume sold of 6.3%.

Commencing July 1, 2025, the minimum percentage of biodiesel that is required be blended with home heating oil sold for heating purposes in buildings located in the States of New York and Connecticut (where a significant portion of our customers are located) was increased from 5% to 10%.
In Rhode Island, the minimum required biodiesel blend increased from 10% to 20%, also commencing July 1, 2025.
As a commodity, the price of the products that we sell is generally impacted by many factors, including economic and geopolitical forces and is closely linked to the price of diesel fuel.
From an inventory cost perspective, backwardation has a discouraging effect on holding physical stocks.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Star uses diesel fuel derivatives to hedge inventory and price-protected volume without hedge accounting, causing non-cash mark-to-market earnings swings such as a $13.4 million credit in fiscal 2025.
quotes: We have opted out of, and do not follow hedge accounting for our commodity derivative instruments as hedging instruments, as a result, the changes in fair value of the commodity derivative instruments are recognized in our statement of operations.

Therefore, we experience volatility in earnings as outstanding derivative instruments are marked-to-market and non-cash gains or losses are recorded prior to the sale of the commodity to the customer.

During fiscal 2025, the change in the fair value of derivative instruments resulted in a $13.4 million credit as a decrease in the market value for unexpired hedges (a $1.0 million charge) was more than offset by a $14.4 million credit due to the expiration of certain hedged positions.

At July 31, 2026, over 92% of the hedges for our ceiling customers were at their strike price (ceiling), which reduces the potential for per gallon margin expansion for these customers unless the price for home heating oil declines.

business_model.basis: stated in P3, P4, and P6
business_model.claim: Delivery and branch expenses ($400.8 million in fiscal 2025) move with acquisitions, delivered gallon volume, insurance costs, and weather hedge contract settlements that required a $5.0 million expense in fiscal 2026.
quotes: For fiscal 2025, delivery and branch expenses increased $34.4 million to $400.8 million, compared to $366.4 million for fiscal 2024.

As a result, as of March 31, 2026, and March 31, 2025, we increased delivery and branch expense and recorded a payable under those weather hedge contracts of $5.0 million and $3.1 million, respectively.

The Company reported a third quarter Adjusted EBITDA loss (a non-GAAP measure defined below) of $17.7 million, up $7.1 million year-over-year, as higher home heating oil and propane per gallon margins, an improvement in service and installation profitability and the additional gross profit from other petroleum products were more than offset by higher operating expenses, including $6.2 million in higher insurance-related expenses, and the lower volume of home heating oil and propane sold.

business_model.claim: Installation and service costs ($110.9 million and $198.2 million in fiscal 2025) depend on acquisitions and service demand under fixed-fee prepaid contracts, while general and administrative expenses ($30.5 million in fiscal 2025) include an accrual of approximately 6.0% of Adjusted EBITDA for employee profit sharing.
quotes: Total installation costs for fiscal 2025 increased by $10.0 million or 9.9%, to $110.9 million, compared to $100.9 million of installation costs for fiscal 2024.
Service expense increased by $15.7 million, or 8.6%, to $198.2 million for fiscal 2025, representing 93.7% of service sales, versus $182.5 million, or 94.2% of service sales, for fiscal 2024.

In addition, a large proportion of our service expenses are incurred under fixed-fee prepaid service contract arrangements, therefore trends in service expenses may not directly correlate to trends in the related revenues.

For fiscal 2025, general and administrative expenses increased $2.1 million, or 7.4%, to $30.5 million, compared to $28.4 million for fiscal 2024, due to a $1.5 million increase in profit sharing expense and a $0.6 million increase salaries and benefits expenses.
The Company accrues approximately 6.0% of Adjusted EBITDA as defined in its profit sharing plan for distribution to its employees.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Higher wholesale product prices also increase credit card fees, bad debt expense, vehicle fuel costs, and working capital borrowings, raising net interest expense ($14.3 million in fiscal 2025).
quotes: Significant increases in product and energy costs result in higher operating expenses, such as credit card fees, bad debt expense, and vehicle fuels, and also lead to higher working capital requirements, including higher premiums and cash requirements for some of our hedging instruments.
For fiscal 2025, net interest expense increased by $2.7 million, or 23.9%, to $14.3 million compared to $11.6 million for fiscal 2024.
Further, interest expense may increase due to higher borrowings to finance higher receivables.
